newsitem.title: USA: El Paso Energy goes nationwide.
newsitem.headline: El Paso Energy goes nationwide.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp said Thursday its $4 billion acquisition of Tenneco Energy has been finalized, creating the nation's first coast-to-coast natural gas pipeline system.

The acquisition from Tenneco Inc was the largest event to date in a plan developed four years ago to transform El Paso from a regulated pipeline system serving a regional market into a company expanding into new markets and shifting more of its activities away from the regulated business arena and into the higher margin, non-regulated parts of the energy industry, chief executive William A. Wise said.

"But this event does not signal the end of transition for our company. Instead, this combination enhances our ability to benefit from the ongoing, dramatic changes taking place in the energy industry," Wise said.

Since being spun off from Burlington Resources in 1992, El Paso has embarked upon an aggressive program to achieve these goals, focusing primarily on areas such as marketing, gathering, processing and international power generation.
The company said it has completed the buyback of more than 4.6 million shares of its common with a value of about $216 million, based on Wednesday's closing stock price of $47.

"Today's acquisition adds an impressive milestone to the list of accomplishments we've completed in the strategic transformation that began when we became a stand alone company just four years ago," Wise said. "It is an excellent fit with the series of actions we've taken to carry out our plans."
Terms of the transaction included the issuance of new El Paso equity totaling about $900 million and the assumption of $2.8 billion of Tenneco debt and preferred stock.
Tenneco common stockholders will receive about 0.93 El Paso common shares for every 10 Tenneco shares held.
